# Hooks for ecommerce videos: 36 openings that make the product matter before the swipe

At 0:02, the product is already in frame—and the viewer has already moved on. The problem is rarely that the item is uninteresting. The opening gave them no reason to stay for the next sentence.

![Three Hook Lab hooks for one video](https://uploads.postiz.com/uO68lfcXhM.png)

This page gives you ready-to-use hooks for ecommerce videos, organized by the job your product needs to do: reveal a problem, show a use, answer doubt, or make a comparison. Pick one that matches the footage you actually have, then test the spoken line and on-screen text together.

## Problem-first hooks

Use these when the buyer recognizes an annoyance before they recognize your product.

1. “If your [problem] keeps happening, look at this.”
2. “I didn’t realize this was causing my [problem] until I tried this.”
3. “The tiny reason your [item or routine] feels harder than it should.”
4. “Still dealing with [problem]? This is the part I changed.”
5. “Nobody tells you that [common product category] can do this.”
6. “This is for anyone tired of [specific frustration].”
7. “I thought [problem] was normal until I saw this side by side.”
8. “Before you buy another [category], check this one detail.”
9. “The thing making your [task] take longer is probably this.”

**On-screen text ideas:** “Fix the annoying part” · “Before you replace it” · “The detail I missed”

## Product-demo hooks

Use these when the transformation can be seen immediately.

10. “Watch what happens when I use this on [surface, item, or situation].”
11. “Here’s [product] doing the one thing I bought it for.”
12. “I’m testing whether this actually works on [real use case].”
13. “This takes [ADD: your time] to set up.”
14. “One hand, one step, and this is the result.”
15. “The satisfying part is what happens next.”
16. “I used this exactly how the instructions say—and here’s the result.”
17. “You can see the difference before I explain it.”
18. “This is what [product] looks like in a normal day, not a studio.”

**On-screen text ideas:** “Real-use test” · “No setup montage” · “See it work”

## Before-and-after hooks

Use these only when your video can honestly show both states.

19. “Before this, my [object or routine] looked like this.”
20. “The before is why I wanted to try it.”
21. “Same [item], one change.”
22. “Here’s the result after [ADD: your duration] of using it.”
23. “I wanted [desired outcome], so I changed this first.”
24. “Left: before. Right: after. Here’s what changed.”
25. “This is the difference one [product or step] made for me.”
26. “Don’t look at the product yet—look at this result.”
27. “The after is nice. The before is the reason it matters.”

**On-screen text ideas:** “Before → after” · “One change” · “Look at the result”

## Comparison hooks

Use these when the buyer is deciding between options or is skeptical of a familiar alternative.

28. “I put this next to the [usual option] so you can see the difference.”
29. “Which one would you choose without knowing the price?”
30. “I expected these to feel the same. They don’t.”
31. “This is the feature I check before buying any [category].”
32. “The cheaper option looked similar—until I used both.”
33. “Two ways to solve [problem]. Here’s why I chose this one.”
34. “What you get with [product] that I couldn’t get from [alternative].”
35. “I compared the part that matters after the first use.”
36. “Before you choose between these, watch this test.”

**On-screen text ideas:** “Side-by-side test” · “Which would you pick?” · “The part that matters”

## How to choose a hook for your ecommerce video

Start with the footage, not a clever sentence. If you have a visible demonstration, choose a product-demo hook. If the value is a relief from an irritating routine, choose a problem-first hook. If buyers hesitate between alternatives, use a comparison hook. If you can document a real change without stretching the claim, use before-and-after.

Then make the first three seconds answer one question: what is happening, and why should this viewer care? Show the product or result while saying the line. A spoken hook with unrelated visuals asks too much of a fast-scrolling viewer.

Keep the first line specific. “This changed everything” gives the viewer nothing to evaluate. “Before you buy another travel mug, check this lid” gives them a reason to see the next shot.

## A simple way to test hooks

Make several openings for the same core video. Change the first spoken line, on-screen text, and first shot; keep the rest of the video as consistent as practical. Compare the results in the platform’s own analytics after each version has a comparable chance to reach viewers.

Test one angle at a time:

- **Problem:** Does the viewer recognize the frustration?
- **Proof:** Can they see the product doing its job?
- **Contrast:** Is there a clear choice or difference to inspect?
- **Curiosity:** Does the opening create a question the next shot answers?

A hook can be direct or surprising. Direct works when the buyer already knows the problem. A more unexpected line can earn attention when the product needs context. Neither is automatically better; the footage and audience decide.

## FAQ

### How long should an ecommerce hook be?

Aim to deliver the premise in the opening seconds. The spoken line should be easy to understand on first listen, while the screen shows the product, problem, or result it refers to.

### Should I show the product immediately?

Usually, yes—especially for a physical product. If the hook names a problem first, show the problem or a relevant close-up so the viewer can connect the claim to something concrete.

### Can I use the same hook for every product?

Use the structure, not the exact sentence. Replace generic phrases with the product’s real use case, buyer objection, and available visual proof.

### What if I do not have a dramatic before-and-after?

Use a demo, comparison, setup, or objection hook. A clear small proof is more useful than an exaggerated transformation.

## What the tool returns

Here is a published example of the kind of brief and structured output Hook Lab returns:

**You send:** "Hooks for a 30s TikTok about why most people quit the gym in January — energetic, for beginners."

**You get back (shortened):**
- **Positioning:** "The gym isn't the problem — your first week is." You own the beginner-who-keeps-quitting angle.
- **Hooks (5+, each with spoken line + on-screen text + type):**
  1. *Contrarian* — 🗣 "Stop going to the gym every day." / 🖥 "Day 1 is where you quit"
  2. *Question* — 🗣 "Why does everyone quit by January 20th?" / 🖥 "The January 20th wall"
  3. *Mistake* — 🗣 "You're not lazy. You're doing week one wrong." / 🖥 "Week 1 mistake"
- **Recommended pick:** #3, with one line on why it fits a beginner audience.
- **Script:** 0–3s hook · 3–10s the mistake · 10–22s the fix in 3 steps · 22–30s CTA.
- **Caption:** short caption + CTA + hashtags, plus one filming tip.
